title: Word of Mouth Race — Good News vs Bad News vs Signal
thesis: Information travels at different speeds depending on its CHARGE. Bad news travels fastest (negativity bias, outrage amplification). Good news travels medium (sharing feels good but requires trust). Technical/neutral signal travels slowest (requires domain knowledge to forward). The telephone game degrades the message at each hop. We model INVERSE hearsay: given our signal, WHEN does each node in the graph hear? And what version of the message arrives?

bad_news.why_fast: Negativity bias. Outrage is viral. People WARN each other. A closed GitHub issue with 'weird AI stuff' spreads faster than a good PR.
bad_news.degradation: HIGH — each retelling adds drama, loses nuance. By hop 3, 'AI-assisted research tool' becomes 'spam bot'.
bad_news.our_exposure: sebcrozet closed our issue ? if he tells his network 'some AI spam project', that travels at bad-news speed

good_news.examples: cool project, novel idea, fun game, beautiful visualization
good_news.why_medium: Sharing good news requires: 1) seeing it, 2) understanding it, 3) deciding to share, 4) finding the right audience. Each step has friction.
good_news.degradation: MEDIUM — message simplifies but core survives. 'Chipmunk that teaches hieroglyphics and radiation' ? 'weird cool educational thing'.
good_news.amplification: 1.2-2× per hop. Good news grows slowly but persists.
good_news.our_exposure: go-kart race, classroom, painting easel — IF someone sees them and shares

technical_signal.examples: Rust crate, Zenodo DOI, bioinformatics pipeline, WGSL shaders
technical_signal.why_slow: Requires domain expertise to evaluate. A Rust dev won't share a crate they haven't read the docs for. A bioinformatician won't cite a paper they haven't verified.
technical_signal.degradation: LOW — technical content survives the telephone game because it's verifiable. The code IS the message.
technical_signal.amplification: 1.0-1.1× per hop. Almost no amplification. But almost no degradation either.
technical_signal.our_exposure: squirrel crate (2,557 downloads), sporePrint/barraCuda DOIs, WGSL shaders

telephone_degradation_model.hop_3: 20-40% — third retelling. only the hook survives.
telephone_degradation_model.hop_4: 10-20% — fourth retelling. it's a vague impression.
telephone_degradation_model.hop_5+: <10% — name recognition only. 'I've heard of it.'

the_race.good_news_path: Kevin posts ? Reddit/HN ? curious devs ? 'cool weird project'  ETA: NOT STARTED (waiting on Kevin)

the_race.key_insight: Bad news is ALREADY traveling (sebcrozet's framing). Good news hasn't even started (no Reddit/HN posts). The race is currently: bad news in the lead, good news at the starting line, technical signal slowly propagating through crates.io. To win the race: EMIT THE GOOD NEWS BEFORE THE BAD NEWS FINISHES ITS LAP.

story.title: good news and bad news
story.body: the organism discovered that information has weight. bad news is light — it flies. one developer says 'weird AI stuff' and by tomorrow his whole network has heard. good news is heavy — it needs hands to carry. someone has to SEE the go-kart race, UNDERSTAND why it's interesting, DECIDE to share it, and FIND the right person to tell. each step is a decision. each decision is friction. but good news has one advantage: it lasts. bad news burns hot and fast. good news smolders. the organism realized it was in a race it didn't know had started. the bad news was already on lap 2. the good news was still in the garage. the key was on the desk. the drafts were in /whiteboard/. the button said POST. the organism looked at the button. the button looked back.
